item.title: Okaloosa County completes Cinco Bayou Boat Ramp upgrades

item.content:encoded:
Okaloosa County and the town of Cinco Bayou are marking the finish line on improvements to the Cinco Bayou Boat Ramp with a ribbon-cutting ceremony planned for late September, according to county officials.

The upgraded facility will serve recreational boaters and anglers in the area, with the county and town working together on the project. Details on the specific improvements and the exact date for the ribbon-cutting event were not immediately available.

The boat ramp serves as a key access point for water recreation in the Okaloosa County area, making the upgrades significant for the local boating community.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County officials have announced that construction work on Pensacola Beach Boulevard will resume next week, bringing lane closures and traffic pattern changes to the busy beach corridor.

According to WKRG News 5, the resumption of construction will affect traffic flow along the boulevard, with drivers advised to expect delays and use alternate routes when possible during peak beach traffic times.

The county has not yet released specific details about which lanes will be closed, the exact start date, or how long the work is expected to last. Commuters heading to Pensacola Beach should monitor local traffic reports and plan extra travel time during the construction period.

Escambia County is expected to provide additional details about the project timeline and traffic management in the coming days.

item.content:encoded:
An upcoming rodeo in Escambia County will combine Western entertainment with a charitable mission to support an equine rescue operation and youth programming at an Elberta ranch.

The event is designed to benefit a local horse rescue while also supporting girls' activities and programming at the ranch facility. Organizers are leveraging the rodeo format—featuring traditional cowboy competitions and entertainment—as a way to draw crowds and generate proceeds for both the rescue mission and youth initiatives.

While specific event dates and venue details were not immediately available from the initial reporting, the rodeo represents a collaborative effort between Escambia County organizations and the Baldwin County horse rescue to raise awareness and funds for animal welfare and youth development in the region.

item.content:encoded: Hurlburt Field has rescheduled planned detonations that were originally set for today, according to Air Force officials. The controlled detonations will now take place Wednesday, September 16, between 7 a.m. and 3 p.m. Air Force representatives cited unfavorable weather conditions as the reason for the postponement. Residents in the surrounding area may experience noise and vibrations during the rescheduled window. The base typically provides advance notice of such operations to minimize disruption to nearby communities.

item.title: Foley pauses new data center projects with 6-month moratorium
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Foley City Council has enacted a temporary halt on new data center applications, according to WKRG News 5. The measure passed its final reading during the council's Sept. 8 meeting, imposing a six-month moratorium on accepting or approving any new data center projects in the city. The moratorium gives city officials time to review existing…
item.content:encoded:
The Foley City Council has enacted a temporary halt on new data center applications, according to WKRG News 5. The measure passed its final reading during the council's Sept. 8 meeting, imposing a six-month moratorium on accepting or approving any new data center projects in the city.

The moratorium gives city officials time to review existing policies and potentially develop new regulations governing how data centers operate within Foley's limits. Data center projects have become increasingly common across the Southeast, raising questions about infrastructure impacts, power demands, and community concerns.

While Foley is just across the state line in Alabama, the decision could have implications for broader regional development patterns. The moratorium will remain in effect for six months unless the council votes to extend or lift it sooner.

item.content:encoded: The Pensacola Blue Wahoos couldn't recover from an early deficit in Wednesday night's game against the Biloxi Shuckers, dropping a 9-2 decision. item.title: Tate Volleyball Falls to Spanish Fort in Straight Sets

item.content:encoded:
The Tate High School Aggies couldn't keep their momentum rolling Wednesday evening, dropping a straight-sets match to visiting Spanish Fort High School in Cantonment. The Toros dominated the contest, winning 25-14, 25-20, 25-14 in what marked a quick turnaround for the Aggies after a strong performance the night before.

Tate had been riding high after picking up a 3-1 victory over Booker T. Washington on Tuesday, but the team ran into a tough test against the Alabama-based Spanish Fort squad. The Toros came into Escambia County and controlled play throughout the evening, showing little struggle in any of the three sets.

The loss drops Tate's record and sets up another opportunity to bounce back in upcoming matches as the volleyball season continues.

item.content:encoded:
The Century Neighborhood Watch is getting back to work this Thursday after taking a summer hiatus. The community group will convene at 5 p.m. at the Century Business Center, located at 150 Pond Street, Suite 5B, marking the restart of regular meetings for the North Escambia area.

The first gathering back will feature a special presentation from the Escambia County Sheriff's Office Narcotics Division, giving residents a chance to hear directly from law enforcement about drug-related concerns and community safety strategies in the region.

Neighborhood Watch members are encouraged to attend and reconnect with fellow residents focused on improving public safety and quality of life in Century.

item.content:encoded:
A wet weather pattern is moving into the Pensacola area, with rain expected to increase Thursday and persist through Sunday, according to the National Weather Service.

Thursday afternoon will see showers and thunderstorms likely between 1 p.m. and 4 p.m., with conditions worsening Friday and Saturday. The heaviest rainfall is expected Friday and Saturday, when locally heavy downpours are possible. A few of the stronger storms could produce strong wind gusts, so residents should monitor conditions closely.

High rain chances are forecast to continue into Sunday as the wet pattern settles over the region. Those with outdoor plans should prepare for frequent showers and thunderstorms over the next several days and consider bringing activities indoors when possible.
